classification.difficultyReason: Choose the applicable chord-midpoint or angle-bisector theorem, then apply the explicitly demonstrated Pythagoras and inverse-sine operations in three supplied figures.

content.prompt: Find the exact value of $x$, as a surd if necessary. Then use trigonometry to find the value of $\theta$, correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Circle with centre O, chord AB and M on AB. OM is perpendicular to AB, with the right-angle marker at M. MB = 4, OB = 5, OM = x and ∠MOB = θ. OA is also drawn.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: Triangle OMB is right-angled at M. By Pythagoras, $x=\sqrt{5^2-4^2}=3$. Also $\sin\theta=\frac{4}{5}$, so $\theta=\sin^{-1}(\frac{4}{5})\approx53.1^\circ$.

spec.description: Circle with centre O and vertical chord ST on the right. B lies on ST; OB is drawn horizontally. Radii OS and OT are drawn. OS = x, SB = 4 and OB = 6. Both ∠SOB and ∠BOT are labelled θ.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: OB bisects $\angle SOT$, so it is perpendicular to chord ST. In right triangle OBS, $x=\sqrt{6^2+4^2}=\sqrt{52}=2\sqrt{13}$. Then $\sin\theta=\frac{4}{(2\sqrt{13})}$, giving $\theta\approx33.7^\circ$.

spec.description: Circle with centre O and horizontal chord LN below O. M lies on LN; matching double ticks mark LM = MN. OM = 4, ON = 8, MN = x and ∠MNO = θ. OM and ON are drawn.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: M is the midpoint of chord LN, so $OM\perp LN$. Thus $x=\sqrt{8^2-4^2}=\sqrt{48}=4\sqrt3$. Since $\sin\theta=\frac{4}{8}=\frac{1}{2}$, $\theta=30.0^\circ$.
